items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the public authorities law and the tax law, in relation to requiring the metropolitan transportation authority to renegotiate the joint service operating agreement with the state of Connecticut
items.lawCode: Amd §1266, Pub Auth L; amd §800, Tax L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S4825

TITLE OF BILL:
An act
to amend the public authorities law and the tax law, in relation to
requiring the metropolitan transportation
authority to renegotiate the joint
service operating agreement with the state of Connecticut

PURPOSE:
To ensure fairness to the residents of the counties of
Dutchess, Orange, Putnam and Rockland by eliminating the Metropolitan
Commuter Transportation tax imposed upon the residents of these four
counties without impairing revenues flowing to the Metropolitan
Transportation Authority.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:
Section one provides the legislative intent, recognizing that under
Chapter 25 of the laws of 2009, Dutchess, Orange, Putnam and Rockland
contribute an excessive amount to support the Metropolitan
Transportation Authority (MTA) and provides a mechanism to relieve
taxpayers of these four counties of the metropolitan commuter
transportation tax, also known as the MTA payroll tax, to create a
more equitable solution without compromising revenues collected for
the support of the MTA.

Section two amends Section 1266 of the Public Authorities law
requiring the MTA to:

(1) renegotiate the joint service agreement between the authority and
the state of Connecticut to require equitable Connecticut fare levels
and require that the Connecticut operating deficit subsidy payments
be based on Connecticut resident utilization of the MTA; or, (2)
reduce services and expenses related to the Metro-North New Haven
line operation by a recurring MTA savings amount which is equivalent
to the increased joint service agreement payments which would
otherwise be determined under renegotiation; or (3) terminate the
Amended and Restated Service Agreement dated June 21, 1984, and any
amendments or modifications thereto, including but not limited to any
and all arbitration opinions and awards, notwithstanding any
provision of this section or any other law to the contrary.

Section three amends Section 800 of the Tax law excluding Dutchess,
Orange, Putnam and Rockland from contributing to the MTA payroll tax
established in Chapter 25 of the laws of 2009 and requiring that tax
revenues previously collected under this section from within the
Counties of Dutchess, Orange, Putnam and Rockland be reimbursed to
each payor by March 31, 2010.

Section four sets an immediate effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:
Chapter 25 of the Laws of 2009 imposed a payroll tax on virtually all
employers in the Metropolitan Transportation Authority 12 county
region. Transit riders in the Counties of Dutchess, Orange, Putnam
and Rockland, however, comprise only one percent of the combined


population of these counties. While these four counties are only
allowed a one-quarter vote on the MTA Board due to their low system
utilization, this same level of minimal utilization was not
recognized when Chapter 25 Was enacted imposing the same 34 cents per
$100 of payroll on employers throughout the MTA region.

As a result of Chapter 25 of the laws of 2009, the counties of
Dutchess, Orange, Putnam and Rockland have been forced to Contribute
more than $90 million in added revenues to the MTA.
The full amount contributed from the four counties is in excess of
$365 million or $32,000 per transit rider.

This legislation recognizes that 26% of the Metro-North transit riders
are Connecticut residents, who were not required to contribute to the
Metropolitan Transportation Authority operating deficit bail-out.
Currently, Connecticut's ridership is estimated at 26,000, providing
a subsidy of $4000 per transit rider. This legislation requires the
MTA to renegotiate the joint service operating agreement between the
Authority and Connecticut to reflect increased fare and subsidy
equity payments based on utilization. If an agreement does not
produce an equitable fare increase and subsidy payments from
Connecticut, the MTA is defected to reduce services to the New Haven
line operation by an amount that produces recurring savings equivalent
to that which would have otherwise been collected through an
equitable agreement.

In an effort to eliminate the payroll tax in the counties of
Dutchess, Orange, Putnam and Rockland and maintain revenue
neutrally, approximately $7 million would be additionally required
resulting in an estimated 13% fare increase among transit riders
in the four counties.

Given the unfair and excessive burden placed on taxpayers in
Dutchess, Orange, Putnam and Rockland counties, this legislation
would also require that tax revenues previously collected from each
payor be reimbursed by March 31, 2010.

This bill is revenue neutral and does not negatively impact the level
of funds flowing to the MTA.  Commuters in New York State outside
of Dutchess, Orange, Putnam and Rockland counties are not affected
by this legislation.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:
2010: S.6267 - Referred to Transportation
2009: S.6267 - Referred to Rules

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:
None to the State or the Metropolitan Transportation Authority.
Dutchess, Orange, Putnam and Rockland counties will benefit from the
elimination of the MTA payroll tax.

EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately.
